messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Interlingua, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Interlingua line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Durante que io cadeva al basse loco, davanti a mi oculos me se offereva qui per longe silentio pareva fioco.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------|-------------------|--------| | Mentre | Temporal conjunction introducing a simultaneous action | Durante | while / during | OK | | ch'i' | Subordinating conjunction “che” + pronoun “io” (contracted) introducing the clause | que | that / while | OK | | rovinava | Verb (imperf. 1st sg) “was falling / moving down” | cadeva | was falling | OK | | in | Preposition indicating direction toward | al | to the | OK | | basso | Adjective “low” | basse | low | OK | | loco | Noun “place” | loco | place | OK | | dinanzi | Adverb / preposition “before, in front of” | davanti | before / in front of | OK | | a | Preposition introducing the indirect object | a | to / at | OK | | li | Definite article, plural “the” (archaic) | *(omitted)* | – | **UNNECESSARY** (article not required in Interlingua) | | occhi | Noun “eyes” | oculos | eyes | OK | | mi | Clitic pronoun 1st sg dative “to me” (here as possessive) | mi | my | OK | | si | Reflexive pronoun used in passive construction | se | itself / oneself | OK | | fu | Auxiliary verb (past remote of *essere*) forming passive | offereva | was offering / was presented | OK | | offerto | Past participle “offered, presented” | offereva | was offering / was presented | OK | | chi | Relative pronoun “who, that” | qui | who / that | OK | | per | Preposition “through, by means of” | per | through | OK | | lungo | Adjective “long” | longe | long | OK | | silenzio | Noun “silence” | silentio | silence | OK | | parea | Verb (imperf. 3rd sg) “seemed” | pareva | seemed | OK | | fioco | Adjective “hoarse, weak” | fioco | hoarse / weak | OK |
### Items flagged - **UNNECESSARY**: *li* – the definite article is omitted in Interlingua because it is not required. No other source words are missing, wrong, or grammatically problematic.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Interlingua script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Interlingua text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
